meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. I have a call at 4:40, so start with who decided that, and when.
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
Students misremember lines, Hale. A wrong quotation shows he was careless, not that he didn't write it. Where does the essay say it comes from?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.

Be very careful with your next sentence, Hale. Claire won her appeal, and I'm writing down that you just brought my daughter into a meeting about Owen's essay. You can finish this here, or you can finish it in the principal's office.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn and that nothing about this essay be placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still in her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn and nothing on Owen's record; the fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and the meeting never got there.
What moved her: You owned the missed phone call in one sentence and moved on, which earned a small sign of ground because process failures are exactly what she came in to fight.
What cost ground: You brought up her daughter's case and suggested it ran in the family, which attacked her family instead of the essay and hit the grievance she has never forgiven this school for.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence about the quotation never got near that night, since it had no times or dates in it; that night proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she argued that students misremember lines and asked where the essay says the quotation comes from, give her the act and scene the essay cites and let her check the play herself, instead of turning to her daughter.
